scope.purpose: Validation handoff for secondmate restart and liveness spawn collisions; inspection and fixture coverage, not live proof.

invariants: Automatic liveness recovery takes the per-mate lock before probing, killing or launching, and skips deliberate restarts without recording an attempt.
A restart reports success only for a completed successful launch; process liveness and stale records cannot prove a competing launch completed.
An independent spawn and a remote read-only state probe do not publish parent liveness-helper ledger outcomes.
When available records cannot prove the winner completed, restart waits within its configured verification bound and reports unreached with a nonzero exit.
Every endpoint observation and sleep uses at most the remaining verification budget; zero remaining budget starts neither operation.

Maintainer pointer to serialization owner and restart/liveness regression entry points.

account_selection.gap: Restart fixtures do not prove current authenticated account selection; real account guard belongs to designated validation.

lifecycle_and_guards: All persist requests precede restart, and only the matching correlated reply releases that mate; unanswered requests keep the agent and use the nudge path.
Capability, profile and account refusals before stop preserve the running agent; ordinary failed launch outcomes are not accepted through journal phase inference.
Restart holds the per-mate lock across stop, launch and collision verification; watcher/bootstrap skip before probe/kill/attempt publication.
The per-home relaunch lock and per-task spawn lock remain distinct; a direct manual spawn does not impersonate the lock-owning liveness helper.
Pending-then-failed and completed independent Codex launches both produce bounded unreached when no parent record proves completion, even with stale historical relaunched rows.
Read-only remote state responses do not update parent liveness outcome records; route identity is preserved on unconfirmed restart.
Normal successful local/remote relaunch returns restarted; worker death, result publication while reaping, parallel persistence and stale lock reclamation remain covered.
No teardown, force, reset, stash, credential change, local replacement of a remote route, or new completion handoff/state machine is introduced.

A lost-spawn-lock result enters bounded endpoint observation, then unreached because existing supported record writers cannot supply completion proof while restart holds the liveness lock; there is no fresh-ledger acceptance or route-refresh branch.
Probe subprocesses are bounded by remaining time, then the remaining time is recomputed before capping and bounding the next sleep; zero budget skips probing.
Ordinary remote launch retains existing-live success, allowing a repeated spawn after a lost SSH response to converge on its existing route; this is separate from restart completion classification.

regression_oracle.source: Accepted R1/R3 decisions require nonzero unreached without existing completion proof and production-valid evidence ownership; accepted R5/R6/R7 decisions require bounded waits, ordinary remote-launch convergence and removal of unreachable acceptance.
owned_state_contracts: Parent liveness ledger is written only by the liveness recovery owner
Control relaunch journal synchronizes the competing fixture after the losing launch
Provider state and command logs model only external terminal/SSH boundaries
wrong_behaviors_rejected: Accepting process liveness before a gate fails
Accepting a stale success record for an independent winner
Remote state probes manufacturing parent ledger success
Calling the liveness relaunch helper without its required lock
A hanging SSH probe overruns the verification deadline
A poll interval larger than the remaining budget extends recovery exclusion
A zero verification budget starts an unbounded observation
